overlayAddress.body: The private address this device uses inside the mesh (100.64.x.x). It only works between enrolled devices, never on the public internet.

posture.body: Whether this device's security checks (disk encryption, firewall, OS version) have been reported and confirmed. "Unverified" means no report has arrived yet, not that the device failed a check.

onion.body: Traffic is relayed through several hops, each one encrypted in its own layer, so no single relay knows both who is asking and what they are asking for.

acl.body: A list of rules that decides which devices may talk to which, by address and port. Zero-trust means nothing is allowed unless a rule says so.

derp.body: A relay server that forwards encrypted traffic between two devices that cannot reach each other directly, for example because both sit behind restrictive firewalls.

quarantine.body: The device is isolated from the rest of the mesh: its traffic is blocked until an operator lifts the quarantine. It stays enrolled; nothing is deleted.

statusBanner.openTitle: No rule is defined — the mesh is open
statusBanner.openDesc: Node enforcement is default-deny, so an empty policy delivered to the fleet would stop all traffic. The control plane compiles allow-all while this table is empty: every node may reach every other. Writing the first rule closes the mesh to everything it does not permit.
statusBanner.enforcedDesc: Network access control rules are compiled into per-peer VIP filters and enforced in the sovereign WireGuard netstack.

defaultPolicyCard.title: Organization Default Policy
defaultPolicyCard.description: Determines how traffic that does not match any specific ACL rule is handled across all mesh nodes.
defaultPolicyCard.openExpl: Unmatched mesh traffic between non-quarantined peers is permitted by default.
defaultPolicyCard.denyExpl: Strict Zero-Trust: all unmatched traffic is silently dropped by the TUN filter.
defaultPolicyCard.confirmDesc: Switching organization default policy to {{policy}} will advance the mesh epoch and immediately alter filtering on all fleet nodes. Are you sure you wish to proceed?

verifyModal.title: Cryptographic Chain Verification Report
verifyModal.subtitle: Mathematical validation of SHA256-HMAC sequential links across the entire audit database.
verifyModal.validDesc: The covered event fields and sequential HMAC links match the stored hashes. Organization attribution is reported separately below.
verifyModal.partialHeadline: CHAIN VERIFIED WITH PARTIAL FIELD COVERAGE
verifyModal.partialDesc: The stored HMAC links match. Older records do not cover all event fields, so changes to fields outside their original format cannot be detected by this check.
verifyModal.unknownDesc: The server reports matching HMAC links. Field coverage is unavailable, so this report cannot confirm that all event fields are protected.
verifyModal.emptyDesc: The audit ledger is empty. There are no event fields or HMAC links to check.
verifyModal.attributionUnavailable: Organization attribution is unavailable or incomplete in this server report.
verifyModal.tamperedDesc: Cryptographic validation failed. An anomaly or unauthorized modification was detected.

checkpointModal.title: Create Cryptographic Checkpoint

nuke.description: Fail-closed cryptographic data obliteration, 4-Eyes dual authorization workflows, legal hold preservation compliance, and Dead Man's Switch controls.

dualAuth.bannerText: Destruction operations require two distinct administrators. The initiator cannot approve their own request, and active legal holds unconditionally abort any shredding action.

requestModal.title: Request Cryptographic Destruction
requestModal.description: Propose an irreversible crypto-shredding operation. A second administrator must approve before execution.

approveModal.title: Approve & Execute Irreversible Destruction
approveModal.warning: CRITICAL WARNING: This action permanently overwrites organization data encryption keys with random cryptographic noise. Decryption of all tenant data and audit records will become physically impossible.
approveModal.holdBlocked: DESTRUCTION BLOCKED: An active legal hold is currently imposed on this target.
approveModal.confirmationPrompt: I certify that I am a distinct administrator and authorize permanent cryptographic obliteration.

legalHolds.bannerText: Imposing a legal hold unconditionally blocks all cryptographic shredding and dead man's switch executions across the specified organization. Holds can only be released by authorized compliance officers.

releaseModal.title: Release Legal Hold

dms.emergencyDesc: Immediately shreds all tenant data, databases, and caches across the entire global mesh.

settings.title: Organisation settings
settings.subtitle: What the control plane applies to this organisation's nodes. A change reaches every node within one heartbeat.
settings.sectionPolicyDesc: Nodes of this organisation only ever peer with each other. Within it, ACL rules decide; with no rule, this policy does.
settings.policyOpen: Open: every node of the organisation reaches every other
settings.policyDeny: Deny: nothing passes without a rule
settings.fieldStalenessHint: How long a node keeps running on its last netmap when it cannot reach the control plane. Past it, the node drops every peer.
settings.stalenessInvalid: Enter a whole number of seconds, 60 or more.
settings.forbidden: Only the organisation's owners and admins can change these settings.
settings.profileRegulatedDesc: The high-risk modules (nuke, deniability, onion) are off and cannot be turned on. Only the platform super-admin can leave this profile.
settings.profileStandardDesc: Feature modules follow their per-organisation switch.
settings.transportBody: WireGuard (wireguard-go). The pre-shared key of each pair rotates every two minutes; it is classical cryptography, not post-quantum. Obfuscation (AmneziaWG) is not active on the nodes, and there is no OpenVPN or VLESS transport.
